```markdown
# Breaking-change flag in release notes

Source: `specs/deferred_items.md` item 7 (picked via /deferred, disposition Design).

## Intent

`release-notes` writes one bullet per merged pull request. Nothing in a bullet
says whether the change is breaking. We want that marked so that:

- people reading the notes can spot breaking changes at a glance, and
- `announce` can put breaking changes first in its post.

`changelog-check` and `announce` both parse `release-notes` output, so they
must accept the new marker.

## Goals

- A bullet for a pull request labelled `breaking` is marked as breaking.
- `changelog-check/parse.py` recognises the marker and records it on the entry.
- `announce` lists breaking entries before the others.

## Non-goals

- No "not breaking" marker. Untagged means not breaking.
- No change to how the rest of a bullet is split or checked.

## Anti-goals

- Older release notes, which have no marker, must not start failing
  `changelog-check`. Untagged bullets parse exactly as they do today.

## Constraints

- `parse.py` splits each bullet on " — " and rejects a bullet with more than
  two parts. This rule stays as it is.

## Approaches

1. **Third part.** Append " — breaking: yes" to the bullet and let `parse.py`
   accept three parts. This loosens the two-part rule, so malformed bullets
   that happen to have three parts would start passing.
2. **Leading tag (picked).** Start the bullet with `[breaking]`. `parse.py`
   reads and strips the tag before it splits, so the two-part rule is
   untouched and untagged bullets parse exactly as before. The tag at the
   start of the line is also what a reader sees first.

Picked: 2, because older notes stay valid and the split rule doesn't change.

## Design

- **`release-notes`** (`skills/release-notes/SKILL.md`): when a merged pull
  request carries the `breaking` label, start its bullet with `[breaking]`
  followed by one space, then the bullet exactly as it is written today.
- **`changelog-check`** (`skills/changelog-check/parse.py`): if a bullet
  starts with `[breaking]`, strip the tag and any following whitespace, then
  split and validate the remainder as today. Set `breaking=True` on the entry;
  every other entry gets `breaking=False`.
- **`announce`** (`skills/announce/SKILL.md`): list entries with
  `breaking=True` before the rest, keeping the original order within each
  group.
- **Test** in `skills/changelog-check/`: one tagged bullet parses with
  `breaking=True` and the same remaining fields as its untagged form; one
  untagged bullet parses with `breaking=False` and unchanged fields.

## Calls made by the designer (not discussed)

- One space after the tag; the parser tolerates any whitespace there.
- The tag is matched only at the very start of the bullet and is
  case-sensitive (`[breaking]`).
- Order within the breaking and non-breaking groups in `announce` is the
  original order.
- `breaking` defaults to `False` on every entry, so code that reads entries
  always finds the field.

## Left to the builder

- How `parse.py` represents the entry field (attribute, dict key) — follow
  the existing entry shape.
- Whether `announce` adds a heading above the breaking group.
```
